lines.trans: These handwritings, are the record of all the details I communicated with Li Mingji's side.
Including every time the phone was hung up, all the questions asked,
And also all the demands Li Mingji raised, I wrote them all on it stroke by stroke.
I just want to ask, these times I put in, will they really have value?
Even if it is as a backup plan.
Actually every time we want to invite some artist, wouldn't it be fine to just ask Ji Xiu from Fentuan Technology?
Why must we every time pretend to let low-level small employees make plans?
Even the lowest-level, smallest employees, also are not willing to waste their own lives for this.
Get out.
Misunderstanding, misunderstanding, misunderstanding.
Just now it was Xingzi calling over, saying Xin Huimei agreed to come participate in the semi-finals,
Guest mentor. Of course because performances are still frozen, for the finals she cannot come.
So the first plan is still Li Mingji.
No need to get out, walk away slowly.

examples.trans: That stroke by stroke is good.
This is wouldn't it be fine.
That wouldn't it be fine is good.
No need to wait for me.

meanings.note: Adverb yě placed strictly before the verb.

examples.trans: This is also a good thing.

meanings.note: Particle le marking completion after a verb or a new situation at the end of a sentence.
Question pronoun shénme; in 没什么 it softens to 'nothing much'.

examples.trans: We need to do the initial artist selection.

meanings.note: Adverb zài for future or repeated actions.

examples.trans: Let's watch it one more time.
I am going to the office tomorrow.

meanings.note: Sentence-final particle ma turning a statement into a yes-no question.
Final particle ba softening suggestions ('let's') or seeking confirmation ('right?').

examples.trans: Do not treat employees like pawns.
The company has many new staff.

meanings.note: Final particle ne asking 'what about X?' or marking ongoing state with 还没.

examples.trans: I still have not finished writing.

meanings.note: Casual farewell huítóu jiàn ('catch you later').

examples.trans: I am going to a meeting first, see you later!

meanings.note: Adverb jiù marking immediacy, 'just/merely', or a direct consequence.

examples.trans: If nobody wants her, she stays.
Of course I am not mentoring her.
I wanted to tell you one thing.
There is lots of work at the company.
Coming — I will pay the bill!

meanings.note: Noun diànhuà; 打电话 means 'make a phone call'.
Structural particle de linking modifiers to nouns.
Ordinal prefix 第 (dì) plus 一 (yī).

examples.trans: Take care of your own health.
We need to run the initial artist selection.
The artist plan must not be leaked.

meanings.note: Passive marker bèi introducing who performed an action.

examples.trans: He was fired by the company.
Do you want this job or not?
Wang Er has to take responsibility.

examples.text: 你让我们的努力白白浪费了。
examples.trans: You made our hard work go to waste.
The teacher asked me to come tomorrow.
How did you think of inviting her?
Today I am treating you to coffee.

meanings.note: Preposition gēn introducing the person you speak or act with.
Adverb hái ('still' in 还没; 'even more' in 还要).

examples.trans: The thesis is still not finished.

meanings.note: Choice conjunction háishi used in either-or questions.

examples.trans: Do you want it or not?
Do you drink tea or coffee?

meanings.note: Inclusive adverb dōu summarizing everything named before it.
